q: A source of electromotive force has an external resistance. (2024)
e: A source of electromotive force inherently possesses an internal resistance rather than an external resistance.

q: Electromotive force is measured in volts. (2024)
e: The SI unit for electromotive force (emf) is the volt (V).

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is the joule. (2024)
e: The practical unit of electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh), whereas the joule is its SI unit.

q: Electromotive force (emf) is the amount of energy provided by the battery per unit charge to move round the complete circuit. (2024)
e: Electromotive force is defined as the total energy supplied per unit charge passing through a complete circuit.

q: The sources of electromotive force convert energy from some other forms into electrical form. (2025)
e: Sources of emf transform chemical, mechanical, or other forms of energy into electrical energy.

q: A battery converts mechanical energy into electrical energy to provide electrical power. (2026)
e: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.

q: Electromotive force is measured in unit of joule (J). (2025)
e: Electromotive force is measured in volts (V), not joules.

q: Electromotive force is not actually a force. (2025)
e: Despite its name, electromotive force represents potential difference or work done per unit charge, not a mechanical force.

q: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. (2025)
e: Transformers increase (step up) or decrease (step down) alternating current (AC) voltages.

q: Electricity is produced by chemical reaction in the battery. (2025)
e: Chemical reactions taking place within the battery cell generate electrical current.

q: The voltage of a battery remains constant regardless of the current drawn from it. (2025)
e: Due to internal resistance within the battery, the terminal voltage drops when current is drawn.

q: Electromotive force is measured in unit of volt (V). (2025)
e: The volt (V) is the standard unit of measurement for electromotive force.

q: When batteries are connected in series, the total voltage is the sum of the individual voltages. (2025)
e: The total voltage of batteries connected in series is equal to the algebraic sum of their individual voltages.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is joule (J). (2025)
e: The practical unit used for electrical energy consumption is the kilowatt-hour (kWh).

q: Electromotive force is not actually a force. (2025)
e: Electromotive force measures energy per unit charge rather than an actual physical force.

q: The material used for fuse should have high melting point. (2025)
e: Fuse wire must have a low melting point so it melts quickly and disconnects the circuit during excessive current flow.

q: Electric stoves change heat energy into electrical energy. (2025)
e: Electric stoves convert electrical energy into heat energy.

q: When a current flows through the nichrome coil, it produces heat energy. (2025)
e: Nichrome wire offers high resistance, which converts electrical energy into heat energy when current passes through it.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is joule (J). (2026)
e: The practical unit of electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour (kWh).

q: A silver filament is used in an electric light bulb. (2025)
e: Tungsten is used for light bulb filaments because of its extremely high melting point.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is kilowatt hour. (2026)
e: Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is the commercial/practical unit used for measuring electrical energy.

q: A small amount of argon is filled in an electric light bulb. (2026)
e: Inert gases like argon are added inside light bulbs to prevent the tungsten filament from evaporating.

q: A fuse wire must be made of a material with a high melting point. (2026)
e: A fuse wire must have a low melting point to safely break the circuit during overcurrent conditions.
